docs.title: Shared terms and artifacts
docs.description: This page names the artifacts we write and shows how each one leads to the next, so a counter clerk's idea can be traced all the way to the release note that tells her it shipped.

visuals.title: What gets made
visuals.caption: Every artifact with a one-line definition and how it connects to the next. Epic is a dashed, optional link.
visuals.alt: Artifact map. Yellow cards, each with a name and one line: Roadmap (published quarterly, one document with five sections); Goal (1-2 years, a change in what people do with a starting value and target); Idea (ongoing, any suggestion from anyone); Initiative (open until the outcome is reached, the tracked bet that an opportunity will move a goal); Solution (one of several tried, tested, built, kept or dropped); Deliverable (committed this quarter, a tangible thing handed over); User story (the smallest piece of value, built in one sprint); Sprint report (each sprint); Release notes; Small request (ongoing, a bounded change under a sprint that does not advance a goal); Discovery brief; Assumption log; Launch readiness check; Enable plan. Labelled arrows connect them: Idea can become Initiative, Initiative is pursued by Solutions, a Solution is sliced into Deliverables, Deliverables are broken into user stories, and so on.

docs.title: Request triage and the idea log
docs.description: Requests reach the team every week, from staff, partners, leadership and the public.

visuals.title: Requests: how they are reviewed
visuals.caption: Every request gets an answer. Some join the roadmap, some are small work, some are a no. Bugs skip triage.
visuals.alt: Flow diagram. A submitted request goes to a weekly team triage review (within 5 business days) with five outcomes: already on the roadmap, link to the roadmap item; small request, add to the small request board; large or strategic, add to the idea log; idea for improvement, add to the idea log; will not do, close it. Every outcome ends with telling the requester. Ideas for improvement go to a product manager review at intake or quarterly planning with three results: mined into an Initiative; future consideration (not yes, not no, and we won't follow up); or closed with the reason. A separate row: a reported bug skips triage and goes to the technical architect, urgent fixes now, otherwise the technical maintenance list. Definitions of each outcome follow below the diagram.

docs.title: Initiatives and solutions
docs.description: An Initiative is the thing we track: a bet that pursuing an opportunity will move a goal, held to the outcome it is meant to change.

visuals.title: Inside an Initiative, until the outcome is reached
visuals.caption: Discover, decide, slice, build, enable, measure. If a Solution doesn't hold up, or the outcome isn't reached, the loop goes back to Discover with another Solution.
visuals.alt: Flow diagram, left to right. An Initiative (hypothesis and outcome measure) feeds step 4 Discover, which produces a discovery brief and an assumption log. A purple decision asks: Solution holds up? No loops back to Discover with another Solution; yes produces a Solution. Step 5 Slice the work produces a story map and Deliverables. Step 6 Build and release (sprints) produces user stories and release notes. Step 8 Enable produces an enable plan and readiness check, feedback to triage, and a Measure the outcome step that updates goal progress. A final decision asks: Outcome reached? Yes closes the Initiative; no goes back to Discover with another Solution.

visuals.title: When it happens: team rhythm
visuals.caption: One example quarter, December to March, with a lane for each cadence: yearly, quarterly, monthly, sprints, ongoing.
visuals.alt: Timeline of one quarter across four months, December to March, in five lanes. Yearly: a direction review (vision, strategy, goals) in early December. Quarterly: quarterly planning (grid, commitments) in mid December, roadmap published in early January, next quarter planning in late March, quarter review (goal progress) at the end of March. Monthly: advisory and steering meetings in late January, February and March. Sprints: six two-week sprints from early January to the end of March, each ending in a sprint review that updates the sprint report. Ongoing: weekly request intake and discovery inside active Initiatives.

templates.title: Roadmap
templates.description: The one document that says where the service is heading and whether it is getting there.

templates.title: Goal
templates.description: A change in what people do, with a starting value and a target, held for one to two years.

templates.title: Idea
templates.description: Any suggestion, from anyone, with no commitment attached.

templates.title: Small request
templates.description: A bounded change to something that already exists, finished in less than a sprint, that doesn't advance a roadmap goal.

templates.title: Initiative
templates.description: The tracked bet that pursuing an opportunity will advance a goal.
templates.changes: Open until the outcome is reached

templates.title: Solution
templates.description: One way the team tries to reach an Initiative's outcome: an output that gets tested, built, kept or dropped.

templates.title: Discovery brief
templates.description: The one-page summary of a round of discovery inside an Initiative: what we set out to learn, who we listened to, which Solutions we considered and what we decided about each.

templates.title: Assumption log
templates.description: The running list of what must be true for a Solution to work, how we tested each assumption, and whether it held.

templates.title: Deliverable
templates.description: A tangible thing handed over, so a commitment can be checked as met or not.

templates.title: Epic
templates.description: A flexible container the team uses to group related user stories.

templates.title: User story
templates.description: The smallest piece of value the team builds, described from the user's side.

templates.title: Sprint report
templates.description: The part of the roadmap updated every sprint: whether the sprint goal was met, where each commitment stands, and what is blocked.

templates.title: Release notes
templates.description: Messages that tell staff, partners and the public what changed, written for the person whose experience changes.

templates.title: Launch readiness check
templates.description: Before a launch, a short go/no-go question to every group the launch affects: are you ready?

templates.title: Enable plan
templates.description: How we make sure people can succeed with what was released: what we teach, who champions it, and how we listen.

overview.title: The system on one page
overview.caption: Eight steps run around one document, the roadmap. Steps 2 and 3 set direction; steps 4 to 8 do the work; what people say comes back in at step 1. Dashed lines show which roadmap section a step updates.
overview.alt: Flow diagram. Eight green step boxes form a loop around a yellow box labelled Roadmap, which lists its five sections: vision and strategy, goal progress, Now Next Later grid, quarterly commitments, sprint report. Clockwise from the left: 1 Capture ideas (ongoing), 2 Set direction (yearly), 3 Plan the quarter (quarterly), 4 Discover (inside an Initiative), 5 Slice the work, 6 Build and release (sprints), 7 Review the sprint (every two weeks), 8 Enable (each launch). Under each step, what it makes. Dashed arrows run from Set direction to roadmap sections 1-2, from Plan the quarter to sections 3-4, and from Review the sprint to section 5. An arrow labelled feedback runs from Enable back to Capture ideas.
